what: *** THE CORDON'S DEATH REGISTERS, WORKED AT LAST ***
the source: full text, surname against the Cordon parish, filtered to its DEATH and BURIAL volumes - 13 October 2026
result: *** THIRTEEN DOCUMENTS, AND THE SEAM IS FINALLY A SIZE A PERSON CAN READ ***
what was already known: The parish was sized on 12 October at about 95 documents across 43 volumes; the four adults of Sarandi 229 were the reason for coming.
what the act says: *** Thirteen of the ninety-five sit in the Cordon's own death and burial books *** - Religious Death Records 1839-1852, 1869-1877; Religious Burial Records 1885-1892, 1892-1897, 1897-1901, 1908-1914 and 1918-1926. *** That is the list, and it is the first time this archive has had one. *** Two were read today; eleven are unread.

what: *** AND THE FIRST ONE OPENED CARRIES A DEATH NOBODY HERE KNEW ***
the source: Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, Religious Death Records June 1869 - February 1877; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-BSFN-Z, *** PLATE READ *** at apid TH-909-52378-67990-19
result: *** TWO SISTERS, AGED FOUR AND THREE, DIED ON THE SAME DAY ***
what was already known: Nothing. Neither child nor their parents were in this register.
what the act says: *** 'En cinco de Agosto de mil ochoc.s sesenta y nueve, MURIERON Vicenta Lavina, de cuatro anos, y Manuela Lavina, de tres anos, hija de D. Xavier (hijo) y de LA FINADA LEONARDA LERENA.' *** Two deaths in one entry, five days into August 1869. *** And the mother was already dead when they died. ***

what: *** WHICH WOULD MAKE IT A DEATH FOR A WOMAN THIS ARCHIVE FOUND ON 12 OCTOBER ***
the source: the same act, against the padron of 1850 read on 12 October
result: *** LEONARDA LERENA WAS DEAD BEFORE 5 AUGUST 1869 ***
what was already known: *** LEONARDA MARGARITA LERENA VEGA, born 20 February 1837 ***, was located on 12 October at casa 229 of Calle Sarandi in the padron of 1850 - entered at eleven, the only white person in a house of four adults who carried the surname by ditto.
what the act says: *** The fit is good and it is NOT a merge. *** The forename is uncommon; the parish is the one she was living in; her daughters were born about 1865 and 1866, when she would have been twenty-eight; and she is dead by 1869, at about thirty-two. *** WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: her own death act, or the girls' baptisms, which would name her parents. *** Neither is found - 'Leonarda Lerena' as a phrase returns ONE document in the whole corpus, and it is this one.

what: *** AND THE FAMILY SHE MARRIED INTO IS NAMED ***
the source: Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records 1857-1860, dispensation *** No. 395 of 1861 *** - ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-VWDN-4, transcript read
result: *** DON XAVIER LAVINA THE ELDER AND DONA MANUELA GOYENECHE ***
what was already known: The 1869 death act calls the father 'D. Xavier (hijo)' - the younger - which implies an elder of the same name and says nothing else about him.
what the act says: *** The dispensation is for a DIFFERENT son: 'Don EMILIO LAVINA Y GOYENECHE, de estado soltero, de edad de veinte y cuatro anos, natural de San Pedro del Durazno ... hijo legitimo de Don XAVIER LAVINA y Dona MANUELA GOYENECHE', marrying Dona Maria Eladia Ramona Mendoza. *** So Leonarda married into a family of Durazno origin, and her husband had a brother. *** A third Lavina record, in the Cordon marriage register of 1866-1872, is Xavier Lavina standing WITNESS at a stranger's wedding in January 1868 - not his own. ***

what: *** AND THE TENTH DISPENSATION STILL DOES NOT EXIST ***
the source: the same dispensation, which surfaced by a route the 12 October sweep did not use
result: *** TESTED AND IT HELD ***
what was already known: On 12 October this archive swept the Montevideo dispensation register on eight compound Lerena forms and concluded there is no tenth Lerena dispensation.
what the act says: *** This one arrived through a surname that is not Lerena at all - LAVINA - and so would have been invisible to that sweep. *** It is *** not *** a Lerena dispensation: the groom is a Lavina y Goyeneche and the bride a Mendoza. *** So the conclusion survives a test it was not designed for, which is worth more than the conclusion was. *** It also shows the shape of the next doubt: a Lerena BRIDE whose dispensation is filed under her husband's surname would be missed by every sweep run so far.

what: *** AND ONE MORE DEATH, NOW AT THE PLATE ***
the source: Cordon, Religious Death Records 1869-1877, entry 619, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-BS82-4 - *** PLATE READ *** 17 October 2026
result: *** AMELIA LERENA, NINE YEARS OLD, DIED 11 NOVEMBER 1871 ***
what was already known: Nothing; she is new to this register.
what the act says: *** 'En once de Nov.e de 1871 murio Amelia Lerena, oriental, de nueve anos. Conste.' *** Born about 1862. *** NO PARENTS ARE NAMED. *** The machine transcript had run her margin into the next entry and set 'Giombalta' beside her; that is the entry below, Juan Giombatta de Tomassi. She is not merged with any Amelia in this register.

what: *** WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR AND NOT FOUND ***
the source: the four adults of casa 229 of Calle Sarandi
result: *** STILL UNFOUND, AND THE FORENAME ROUTE IS TOO WIDE ***
what was already known: Estanislada, Sinforiano, Manuela and Rosa carry the surname by ditto in 1850; the holder formula was swept on 12 October and does not reach them.
what the act says: *** 'Estanislada' alone, with a Cordon place filter, returns NINE PAGES *** - about nine hundred documents - so the forename is not a handle either, and the compound forms return nothing. *** ALL THIRTEEN DEATH AND BURIAL PAGES THAT FULL TEXT RETURNS ARE NOW OPENED (17 October 2026) AND NONE OF THE FOUR IS IN THEM. *** That is a limit on the instrument, not a null on the books: each of the thirteen is the one PAGE where full text saw the surname, not the volume it sits in, and a name written without LERENA, or spelled so the machine missed it, is not on that list.

what: *** ELEVEN MORE PAGES OPENED ON 17 OCTOBER, AND THE FOUR ARE STILL NOT IN THEM ***
the source: full text, the parish's DEATH and BURIAL volumes - the other eleven of the thirteen pages, each opened in the signed-in viewer, with the plate read for six
result: *** ELEVEN LERENA ACTS, ONE ON EACH PAGE, AND SEVEN OF THE PEOPLE ARE NEW TO THIS ARCHIVE ***
what was already known: Two of the thirteen had been read; the rest were a list.
what the act says: *** The plate was read for the acts below that say so; the others are the machine transcript and are labelled. *** Estanislada, Sinforiano, Manuela of Africa and Rosa are in none of them. What the pages held instead is below: a man buried under his father's surname, a woman of eighteen born out of wedlock, a married couple and a widow, and the death of a husband who had been dead twenty-seven years when this archive thought him alive.

what: *** A YOUNG MAN BURIED AS A LARRANAGA, WHOSE MOTHER WAS A LERENA ***
the source: Cordon, Religious Burial Records June 1885 - August 1892, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-4SWL-D - *** PLATE READ ***
result: *** JOSE MARIA LARRANAGA, TWENTY-TWO, BURIED 2 AUGUST 1890 ***
what was already known: Nothing. The Lerena is his mother's, so no search on the surname would have reached him.
what the act says: *** 'En dos de Agosto del ano mil ochocientos noventa se mando dar sepultura eclesiastica al cadaver de Jose Maria Larranaga, oriental, soltero, de veintidos anos de edad, hijo legitimo de Benito Larranaga y de Martina Lerena. Fallecio ayer.' *** Three people are new: him, his father Benito and his mother MARTINA LERENA. Nothing places her in a Lerena family here, and nothing is merged.

what: *** A MARRIED COUPLE FROM SAN JOSE AND TRINIDAD WAS IN THE CORDON ***
the source: Cordon, Religious Burial Records June 1885 - August 1892, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-4SW7-N - *** PLATE READ ***; confirmed by the civil act, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-K97X-Z
result: *** SERVANDO TOMAS GONZALEZ, 'CASADO CON ESTEFANA LERENA', BURIED 25 MAY 1892 - CONFIRMED AS THE SAN JOSE AND TRINIDAD SERVANDO ***
what was already known: The register holds a Servando Gonzalez and an Estefania Lerena at San Jose and Trinidad, with children indexed GONZALEZ LERENA, found on 11 October.
what the act says: *** 'En veinte y cinco de Mayo de mil ochocientos noventa y dos se manda dar sepultura eclesiastica al cadaver de Servando Tomas Gonzalez, oriental, casado con Estefana Lerena, ... cinco anos.' *** The first reading of this row called it a candidate. *** THE CIVIL ACT BELOW SETTLES IT. ***

what: *** A WOMAN OF EIGHTEEN, BORN OUT OF WEDLOCK, NAMED FOR HER MOTHER ***
the source: Cordon, Religious Burial Records June 1885 - August 1892, image 252 of 255, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-4S93-D - *** PLATE READ ***
result: *** SARA LERENA, 'HIJA NATURAL DE TERESA LERENA', BURIED 18 AUGUST 1892 ***
what was already known: Nothing; she and her mother are new.
what the act says: *** 'En diez y ocho de Agosto de mil ochocientos noventa y dos se mando dar sepultura eclesiastica al cadaver de Sara Lerena, soltera, hija natural de Teresa Lerena, orientales, que fallecio hoy de diez y ocho anos de edad.' *** *** HER SURNAME IS HER MOTHER'S, because 'natural' means no father is entered. *** Born about 1874. Neither is placed in a Lerena family here.

what: *** THE 1896 DEATH OF PEDRO A. LERENA IS ALSO IN THE BURIAL BOOK ***
the source: Cordon, Religious Burial Records August 1892 - May 1897, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-49R4-Y - machine transcript only
result: *** BURIED 8 NOVEMBER 1896, AGED SIXTY-NINE, 'CASADO CON MANUELA LEMOS' ***
what was already known: His civil death registration of 7 November 1896 (acta 353) was read at the plate on 12 October.
what the act says: *** It agrees with the civil act on name, age and wife and adds nothing. *** The burial says 'fallecio ayer' on the 8th; the civil act says he died on the 6th, so the word is not a date.

what: *** THE WIDOW OF 1901 IS TERESA LEONARD, AND THE CORDON CLERK WROTE HER SURNAME LEONOR ***
the source: Cordon, Religious Burial Records May 1897 - November 1901, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-49TQ-6 - *** PLATE READ ***; confirmed by the civil act, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-K9Q8-D
result: *** 'TERESA LEONOR DE LERENA', WIDOW, BURIED 27 AUGUST 1901 - CONFIRMED AS THE WIFE OF PEDRO ANTONIO LERENA AND MOTHER OF MANUEL ***
what was already known: The register held a Teresa Leonard, wife of Pedro Antonio Lerena and mother of Manuel Lerena Leonard, with no record of her own; the burial was first filed as a candidate.
what the act says: *** The burial entry says 'Teresa Leonor de Lerena, oriental, de sesenta [y ...] anos, viuda de [forename left blank] Lerena. Fallecio hoy.' *** The civil act of the same day, next row, settles it. The first reading took LEONOR for a given name; it is the clerk's spelling of her surname.

what: *** JULIA JUANICO'S BURIAL GIVES HER AGE FIVE YEARS WRONG ***
the source: Cordon, Religious Burial Records April 1908 - May 1914, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-49PS-Q - *** PLATE READ ***
result: *** BURIED 12 JULY 1910 AS 'JULIA JUANICO DE LERENA ... DE SESENTA Y DOS', WIDOW OF LUIS LERENA LENGUAS ***
what was already known: Her death of 11 July 1910 was read at the plate on 12 October, and her baptism of 1842 on 21 September.
what the act says: *** The day and the widowhood agree. The age does not: her baptism makes her sixty-seven. *** A burial entry's age is the priest's, not a second birth year. Her son Enrique's burial of 17 May 1914, aged forty-one, is on a second page of the same book and agrees with his civil act.

what: *** MANUELA LEMOS'S BURIAL NAMES THE WRONG HUSBAND ***
the source: Cordon, Religious Burial Records February 1918 - October 1926, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-4S3R-S - machine transcript only
result: *** BURIED 24 JULY 1918, AGED SEVENTY-SEVEN, 'VIUDA DE CARLOS LERENA' ***
what was already known: Her husband is Pedro A. Lerena, dead in 1896; Carlos Teodoro is one of her sons.
what the act says: *** She died about 23 July 1918, born about 1841. *** The entry gives her husband as Carlos, not Pedro; the 1896 civil act is the stronger source and the discrepancy is left standing.

what: *** A HUSBAND WHO HAD BEEN DEAD TWENTY-SEVEN YEARS ***
the source: Cordon, Religious Burial Records February 1918 - October 1926, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-4SHT-C - plate read for the date
result: *** CARLOS ALBERTO FEIN, SEVENTY-FIVE, 'CASADO CON ADELINA LERENA', BURIED 18 MAY 1919 ***
what was already known: He was entered only as the husband named on his wife's death registration of 20 November 1946, and a date-reading tool took that as placing him alive in 1946.
what the act says: *** He died about 17 May 1919, born about 1844. *** The 1946 registration names him as her husband without saying he was dead; it is not evidence that he was alive.

what: *** A SECOND LERENA WOMAN MARRIED TO A MAN OF SEVENTY-SEVEN ***
the source: Cordon, Religious Burial Records February 1918 - October 1926, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-49BP-V - machine transcript only
result: *** JOSE MARIA REYES, 'CASADO CON MARIA LERENA', BURIED 13 JUNE 1920 ***
what was already known: Nothing; both are new.
what the act says: *** 'Se mando dar sepultura eclesiastica al cadaver de Jose Maria Reyes, oriental, de setenta y siete anos, casado con Maria Lerena; fallecio ayer.' *** The transcript has not been checked at the plate. No tie is claimed to the Maria Lerena of the 1908 enrolment card.

what: *** THE EARLIEST BOOK GIVES NOTHING THAT WAS NOT ALREADY HELD ***
the source: Cordon, Religious Death Records October 1839 - January 1852, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-BSXL-R - machine transcript
result: *** CARMEN LERENA, THREE, BURIED 14 AUGUST 1841 ***
what was already known: Her act was read at the plate on 20 September 2026 off the cemetery's own register, and her father Justo Lerena and mother Juana Quintana are already rows.
what the act says: *** This is the same act on a second film, with the same priest. *** The page opened has the Names panel read 'Carmen Lerena Lerena', which is the machine doubling the surname that the earlier plate reading already rejected.

what: *** THE LARRANAGA FAMILY IS A FAMILY NOW, AND THE MOTHER IS A LERENA OF ABOUT 1846 ***
the source: Montevideo, Death Records 1884-1886, the civil act of 29 March 1885, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-Z9LY-F - *** PLATE READ *** - found by an exact-phrase full-text search on 'Martina Lerena', four results
result: *** BENITO LARRANAGA, SPANISH, SEVENTY, DIED 28 MARCH 1885, 'CASADO CON DONA MARTINA LERENA, ORIENTAL, DE TREINTA Y NUEVE ANOS' ***
what was already known: Both were named only, on the Cordon burial of their son in August 1890.
what the act says: *** Seven children are named: Benito, Carmen, Jose Maria, Ygnacio, Donato, Doroteo and Antonia. *** He died at 3 a.m. in calle Defensa 22, five years before the son's burial. Martina is born about 1846 and is a Lerena by birth - and her own baptism is NOT in the record index for 1840-1852 and no act gives her parents, so she is still unplaced. Six siblings are new rows, named only.

what: *** AND THE SON'S OWN CIVIL ACT GIVES HIM A TRADE AND A DEATH ***
the source: Montevideo civil death registration no. 121 of 2 August 1890, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2C-K3NM-S - *** PLATE READ *** (no machine transcript exists for this image)
result: *** JOSE MARIA LARRANAGA, A COACHMAN OF TWENTY-TWO, DIED OF CONSUMPTION ON 1 AUGUST 1890 ***
what was already known: His burial at the Cordon, read earlier the same day.
what the act says: *** 'ha fallecido Jose Maria Larranaga ... de veintidos anos ... de estado soltero y de profesion cochero, a consecuencia de tisis pulmonar, segun consta del certificado del Dr. Lisazo' *** at 18 de Julio 847, ten-thirty in the morning, 'hijo legitimo de Benito Larranaga y de Martina Lerena'. The burial and the civil act agree on name, age and parents.

what: *** THE SAN JOSE COUPLE'S CHILDREN, FROM THE INDEX - AND THEN THE ACT ***
the source: FamilySearch record index, surname Gonzalez Lerena with the father's forename Servando, Uruguay - 17 October 2026, *** INDEX ONLY ***
result: *** CHILDREN BORN 1854 TO 1872, AND TWO SONS DEAD AT MONTEVIDEO ***
what was already known: The 1892 burial had been filed as a candidate for the couple, with nothing to test it.
what the act says: *** Servando Cecilio died at Montevideo on 11 October 1911 and Leopoldo, father of Juan Carlos Gonzalez Lerena, on 17 June 1922; the index children were born before May 1892. *** The test was then overtaken: the civil act of 25 May 1892, next row, names Estefania Lerena and nine children, and the candidate is confirmed. Three index-level rows from this row remain; the 1930-32 doubt written here is retracted - those cards are the daughters.

what: *** THE SAN JOSE COUPLE WERE AT TRINIDAD, FLORES, IN 1858 AND 1884 ***
the source: Santisima Trinidad marriage of 20 February 1884, index ark 1:1:XS6J-DWBY - *** INDEX ONLY ***
result: *** ESPERANZA GONZALEZ, 26, MARRIED DAMASO NEGROTTO; HER PARENTS ARE SERVANDO SANTA MARINA GONZALEZ AND ESTEFANIA LERENA ***
what was already known: Corina Francisca's christening at Trinidad in 1858 had 'Nefania' and Servando Gonzalez as parents, unattached.
what the act says: *** The family lived at Trinidad from 1858 to 1884, and two sons later died at Montevideo. *** It does not test the 1892 burial any further, because it says nothing of where Servando was in 1892. A computer-indexed record; a family-tree user has attached it to a 'Estefania Lerena Fernandez, born 1832', which is unsourced and not used.

what: *** THE 1858 BAPTISM NAMES HER, AND THE INDEX HAD LOST HER SURNAME ***
the source: Santisima Trinidad, Baptism Records October 1857 - August 1866, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3HW-7 - *** PLATE READ ***
result: *** CORINA FRANCISCA GONZALEZ, BORN 24 JULY 1858, 'HIJA LEGITIMA DE SERVANDO GONZALEZ Y DE ESTEFANIA LERENA, ORIENTALES' ***
what was already known: The index gave her mother only as 'Nefania' and she was a probable child of the couple.
what the act says: *** She is confirmed as theirs, and the surname Lerena is in the act itself. *** It adds no parent for Estefania, and it does not test the 1892 burial; it fixes the household at Trinidad in 1858.

what: *** THE CIVIL ACT OF 25 MAY 1892 NAMES HER, AND HIS PARENTS, AND NINE CHILDREN ***
the source: Montevideo, Death Records 1892, act no. 194, Seccion 7a, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-K97X-Z, index ark 1:1:6KRL-51CG - *** PLATE READ *** - found by the record-index search for the couple, not by the Cordon full-text list
result: *** SERVANDO TOMAS GONZALEZ, SIXTY-FIVE, 'CASADO CON DONA ESTEFANIA LERENA, DE 60 ANOS', DIED 24 MAY 1892 AT CALLE 18 DE JULIO 541A ***
what was already known: A burial at the Cordon, read earlier the same day, that could only be a candidate.
what the act says: *** Of aortic valve disease; 'hijo legitimo de Don Juan Nepomuceno Gonzalez y de Dona Manuela Muniz, ambos orientales y fallecidos'. *** His wife is Estefania Lerena, oriental, born about 1832, and the children are 'Servando, Esperanza, Corina, Francisco, Carmen, Leopoldo, Leonidas, Estefania y Maria'. *** Declared by his son-in-law Damaso Negrotto, thirty-seven, and by his son LEOPOLDO GONZALEZ LERENA, twenty-nine, a lawyer, who signed. *** Seven rows are new: his parents and five of the nine children, three of whom are only probably the people the index calls Eusebio Leonidas, Estefania Fausta Leopoldina and Maria Bernarda. STILL NOT FOUND: Estefania's own parents.

what: *** HER CIVIL ACT: BORN IN MONTEVIDEO, A WIDOW, WITH HER MOTHER ALIVE AT EIGHTY-TWO IN THE SAME HOUSE ***
the source: Montevideo, Death Records 1901, act no. 252, Seccion 7a, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-K9Q8-D, index ark 1:1:6KRY-C5KY - *** PLATE READ *** - found by the record-index search for the pair Teresa + spouse Pedro Lerena
result: *** TERESA LEONAR DE LERENA, 60, VIUDA DE PEDRO ANTONIO LERENA, DIED 27 AUGUST 1901 AT CALLE PARTICULAR 6 ***
what was already known: She was a name on her son's records and nothing else.
what the act says: *** 'hija legitima de Antonio Leonar ..., fallecido, y de Manuela Iturriaga, de 82 anos, viuda, oriental, con domicilio en la misma casa del suceso; ... quedando del matrimonio un hijo llamado: Manuel.' *** Of endocarditis. Declared by Manuel Lerena, a soldier of about thirty-eight, and Eduardo Epifanio Alvarez. Three rows are new: her father, her mother and her husband. *** THE HUSBAND IS DEAD BY AUGUST 1901 AND HE IS NOT THE PEDRO OF 1896 - the next row shows it. ***

what: *** PEDRO LERENA VEGA WAS BORN ON 1 DECEMBER 1828, AND HIS NAME IS PEDRO ANTONIO NATALIO ***
the source: Nuestra Senora del Carmen la Mayor (the Cordon), Baptism Records November 1828 - December 1836, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-C9YR-D, index ark 1:1:6D3Z-QX4L - *** PLATE READ *** - found as a side result of the index search for Pedro Antonio Lerena with spouse Teresa
result: *** 'BAUTICE SOLEMNEMENTE A PEDRO ANTONIO NATALIO, QUE NACIO EL DIA PRIMERO DEL CORRIENTE, HIJO LEGITIMO DE DN PEDRO ANTONIO LLERENA, NATURAL DE CANELONES, Y DE DA VICENTA VEGA, NATURAL DE MONTE VIDEO' ***
what was already known: A son of Pedro Antonio Lerena and Vicenta Vega, entered at sixteen in the 1850 padron, so labelled 'b. c.1834'.
what the act says: *** The label is corrected to 1828 (no URL moves). *** The census age was six years late. He carries ANTONIO in his own name, which made him a candidate for Teresa Leonar's husband - and the 1864 christening of her daughter, next row, rules that out. The act also calls his FATHER 'natural de Canelones', where the register has the father born at Montevideo in 1793 - a conflict left standing.

what: *** TERESA LEONAR'S DAUGHTER'S BAPTISM SAYS WHO HER HUSBAND'S PARENTS WERE - AND THEY ARE NOT VICENTA VEGA ***
the source: Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion, Baptism Records Dec 1859 - Dec 1864, the christening of 30 April 1864, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-Y3CH-R, index ark 1:1:6D7Z-C7WS - *** PLATE READ *** - found from the Teresa + Pedro Lerena marriage-side index search
result: *** MANUELA, BORN 9 APRIL 1864, 'HIJA LEGITIMA DE PEDRO LERENA Y DE TERESA LEONAR. ABUELOS PATERNOS PEDRO Y MARIA PEREYRA. MATERNOS ANTONIO Y MANUELA BARRIAGA' ***
what was already known: The 1901 civil act gave Teresa one son and a husband Pedro Antonio Lerena; Pedro Lerena Vega, with Manuela Lemos, died in 1896 and carries Antonio in his baptismal name.
what the act says: *** THE TWO PEDROS ARE TWO MEN: *** Teresa's husband is the son of Pedro and MARIA PEREYRA, and Pedro Lerena Vega is the son of Pedro Antonio and VICENTA VEGA. *** The index put this christening at La Union; the volume is the Catedral's. *** Teresa had a DAUGHTER, Manuela, named for her own mother, who stood as godmother; the 1901 act does not list her. Three rows are new. Teresa's husband's father 'Pedro' has no surname in the act and is not identified.

what: *** ESTEFANIA'S PARENTS ARE NAMED: ALEJANDRO AND MARGARITA FERNANDEZ ***
the source: San Jose de Mayo, Baptism Records, folio 198, the christening of Cesarea, April 1872, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-C9L8-H, index ark 1:1:6D34-MGLC - *** PLATE READ ***; found by the record-index search for the couple as parents, in the Catholic Church Records collection
result: *** 'HIJA LEGITIMA DE DON SERVANDO GONZALEZ Y DONA ESTEFANIA LERENA, NATURAL DE ESTA VILLA. AB. PT. D. JUAN Y DA. MANUELA MUNIZ: MAT. DN. ALEJANDRO Y DA. MARGARITA FERNANDEZ' ***
what was already known: Estefania Lerena was a wife and a mother of nine with no parents known; the Trinidad kindred had three children for Alejandro and Margarita.
what the act says: *** THE PAIRING IS STRONG, AND A SECOND ACT - the Trinidad baptism of 1867, act 303, plate read - NAMES THE SAME GRANDPARENTS, 'Maternos Alejandro y Margarita Fernandez', with a godmother ALEJANDRINA LERENA. IT WAS NOT PROVED UNTIL HER OWN BAPTISM WAS READ - SEE THE LAST ROW. ***  the act gives no surname for the grandfather, and the identification with Alejandro Lerena the elder and Margarita Fernandez Alvarez rests on the names, the Fernandez, and San Jose as the birthplace of both. Servando's parents Juan and Manuela Muniz agree with the 1892 act. Socorro is of the same age, about 1832; [THE TWIN AND YOUNGER-SISTER READINGS ARE SUPERSEDED BY HER OWN BAPTISM - see the last row.] The index shows several dates (1890 to 1919) on the children's Catholic entries that cannot be right for a mother born about 1832, probably mis-keyed and the Cesarea record as born 1871; the plate says 25 February 1872.

what: *** THE KINDRED GAINS A SISTER, A BIRTH DATE AND A THIRD DOCUMENT FOR ITS PARENTS ***
the source: San Jose baptism 7 March 1829, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D95F-H; Trinidad death acts 1892 (no. 49), ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-W748-Y, and 1921 (no. 116), ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2H-5W3D - *** ALL PLATE READ ***; found by a record-index search for Alejandro Lerena and Margarita as parents, births 1826-1840
result: *** MARIA LERENA DE FERNANDEZ, 64, DIED AT TRINIDAD ON 3 MAY 1892, A DAUGHTER OF ALEJANDRO LERENA AND MARGARITA FERNANDEZ; ALEXANDRO FLORENCIO WAS BORN AT SAN JOSE ON 23 FEBRUARY 1829; SOCORRO DIED AT 88 AND NAMED ALL FOUR GRANDPARENTS ***
what was already known: The elder couple's children were Socorro, Alejandro the younger and Bernabe, from the dispensations of 1854-58, and Estefania, probably, from two baptisms.
what the act says: *** FIVE CHILDREN, AND THE BAPTISM OF 1829 AND THE ACT OF 1921 BOTH NAME RAMON AND MARIA GONZALEZ AS THE ELDER ALEJANDRO'S PARENTS. *** Maria is new [her husband is Ramon Fernandez - see the last row]. A godmother Clara Llerena stood in 1829. The index mis-keys the 1829 birth as 1823. Estefania's age (60 in 1892) and Socorro's (88 in 1921) make Estefania the elder by a year or less, AND HER OWN BAPTISM, READ ON 18 OCTOBER 2026 (the last row), SHOWS SHE IS THE OLDER SISTER BY ABOUT TWENTY MONTHS - NOT A TWIN.

what: *** TERESA LEONARD AND PEDRO A. LERENA ASKED FOR TWO BANNS TO BE DISPENSED IN JUNE 1861 ***
the source: Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records, expediente no. 422, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-VWNG-D (tail on 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-VWH2-3) - *** PLATE READ ***; found by a FULL-TEXT search for the two names, filtered to Uruguay
result: *** 'DON PEDRO A. LERENA ... HABIENDO CONCERTADO CONTRAER MATRIMONIO ... CON DONA TERESA LEONARD, PARROQUIANA DE LA MATRIZ ... LA MADRE DE LA CONTRAYENTE PASO AL CAMPO A ASISTIR UNA HIJA ENFERMA ... LA DISPENSA DE DOS CONCILIARES PROCLAMAS' ***
what was already known: The marriage of the couple was not indexed under any spelling; only their daughter's 1864 christening and Teresa's 1901 death act had named them.
what the act says: *** DECREE OF 8 JUNE 1861, CONFIRMED BY THE VICARIO'S REGISTER OF DISPENSATIONS (no. 422): GRANTED, TO 'DON PEDRO ANTONIO LERENA'. *** It dates the marriage to June 1861 or soon after, at the Matriz, and shows Teresa had a SISTER - ill in the country - whom no other record names. It does not give Pedro's age or parents, so his father 'Pedro' is still unidentified. The Marriage act itself is still not found.

what: *** A SECOND PEDRO A. LERENA, WITH A WIFE TRINIDAD MORALES, BAPTISED A DAUGHTER AT THE CORDON ON 8 FEBRUARY 1863 ***
the source: Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor (the Cordon), Baptism Records May 1855 - December 1865, folio 440, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-C95P-V - *** PLATE READ *** - found by a full-text search for the petition's own forms, 'Pedro A. Lerena' and 'Teresa Leonard'
result: *** 'AMELIA, NACIDA EL DOS DE MAYO ULTIMO, HIJA LEGITIMA DE D. [PEDRO] A. LERENA Y DE DA. TRINIDAD MORALES, ORIENTALES. PADRINOS D. MAXIMO RIVAS Y DA. AMELIA LERENA' ***
what was already known: Pedro A. Lerena was one name in the register, with two women attached - Teresa Leonard and Manuela Lemos.
what the act says: *** HE IS A THIRD HOUSEHOLD: *** a Pedro A. Lerena with a wife Trinidad Morales in 1862-63, while Teresa Leonard's husband Pedro Antonio is married to Teresa in 1861 and 1864. Pedro Lerena Vega is the best candidate for the Cordon father, with a first wife before Manuela Lemos - NOT MERGED. The godmother is a LERENA, 'Amelia', not the 'Serena' of the index.

what: *** ESTEFANIA'S OWN BAPTISM AND SOCORRO'S: BOTH FOUND AT SAN JOSE, 1831 AND 1832 - AND ESTEFANIA IS THE OLDER ***
the source: San Jose de Mayo, Baptism Records 1828-1836, film 008143327: act 149 (image 57, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D95D-Y) and act 499 (image 102, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D9PY-G) - *** PLATES READ ***; found by stepping through the volume image by image and scanning each image's machine index, because the record index and full text had not returned them
result: *** 'ANA ESTEFANIA, DE QUINCE DIAS DE EDAD, HIJA LEGITIMA DE ALEJANDRO LERENA Y DE MARGARITA FERNANDEZ' (22 JANUARY 1831); 'MARIA DEL SOCORRO, QUE NACIO EL VEINTI...MO DE SEPTIEMBRE, HIJA LEGITIMA DE ALEXANDRO [LERENA] Y DE MARGARITA FERNANDEZ. ABUELOS PATERNOS RAMON LERENA Y MARIA GONZALEZ' (30 OCTOBER 1832) ***
what was already known: Estefania's parents were an identification on two grandparent lines (1867 and 1872), and Socorro's birth was an age.
what the act says: *** ESTEFANIA, BORN ABOUT 7 JANUARY 1831, IS A DAUGHTER OF ALEJANDRO LERENA AND MARGARITA FERNANDEZ BY HER OWN BAPTISM; SOCORRO WAS BORN IN LATE SEPTEMBER 1832, ABOUT TWENTY MONTHS LATER. NOT TWINS. *** The sibship is Maria (about 1827-28), Alejandro (February 1829), Estefania (January 1831), Socorro (September 1832) and Bernabe (10 June 1836, found the same day - next row), spaced about two years apart until Bernabe, nearly four years after Socorro. The index had indexed Estefania's baptism as 'Lorena'; the machine index of the image listed 'Jandro, Lorena, Marga...' and the plate did the rest.

what: *** BERNABE'S BAPTISM: BORN 10 JUNE 1836 AT SAN JOSE, WITH BOTH SETS OF GRANDPARENTS NAMED ***
the source: San Jose de Mayo, Baptism Records 1828-1836, film 008143327, image 203, act no. 1256, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D9PN-8 - *** PLATE READ ***; the same image-by-image scan that found his sisters
result: *** 'BAUTICE ... A BERNABE, QUE NACIO EL DIA DIEZ DEL MISMO MES, HIJO LEGITIMO DE D.N ALEJANDRO LERENA Y DE DA. MARGARITA FERNANDEZ. ABUELOS PATERNOS RAMON Y MARIA GONZALEZ. MATERNOS JUAN Y BARBARA SOTURA' (20 JUNE 1836) ***
what was already known: Bernabe's birth was 'about 1835' from his age in 1897, and the 1911 index said 1836.
what the act says: *** THE YOUNGEST OF THE FIVE, BORN 10 JUNE 1836. *** Godfather Paulino Larriera, a surname shared with the Larriera family of San Jose that Alberto Lerena married into; godmother Dolores Morales; neither is placed and no tie is claimed. Every child of Alejandro and Margarita is now documented by a baptism of his or her own including Maria, whose baptism as Maria Casilda (11 April 1827, in the volume before) is the next row.

what: *** THE ELDEST: MARIA CASILDA, BAPTISED AT SAN JOSE ON 11 APRIL 1827, IS THE MARIA OF THE 1892 DEATH ACT ***
the source: San Jose de Mayo, Baptism Records 1822-1828, film 008163861, image 792 of 815, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-CS9R-5 - *** PLATE READ ***; found because the machine index of the first image I opened in that volume listed 'Alexandro Serena', 'Margari' and 'Maria Casilda Serena'
result: *** 'EN ONCE DE ABRIL DE MIL OCHOCIENTOS VEINTE Y SIETE ... BAUTICE SOLEMNEMENTE A MARIA CASILDA, HIJA LEGITIMA DE ALEXANDRO LERENA Y MARGARITA FERNANDEZ. ABUELOS PATERNOS RAMON Y MARIA DE LEON. MATERNOS JUAN [Y] BARBARA SOTURA. PADRINOS MARCOS DE LEON GONZALEZ Y [MARIA] FERNANDEZ ALBAREZ' ***
what was already known: Maria, the eldest of the five, was known only from her 1892 death act - 'Maria Lerena de Fernandez, sixty-four, a widow' - and her baptism was thought to precede the volume.
what the act says: *** NO BIRTH DATE IS WRITTEN, SO SHE WAS BORN ON OR BEFORE 11 APRIL 1827 AND WAS SIXTY-FIVE IN MAY 1892. *** The identification is STRONG, NOT PROVED: the same two parents and the same four grandparents, and the only Maria of Alejandro and Margarita. The godmother is Margarita's own sister Maria Fernandez Albarez; the godfather Marcos de Leon Gonzalez is kin of the paternal grandmother 'de Leon'. 'Maria de Leon' of this act and 'Maria Gonzalez' of her brothers' acts are almost certainly one grandmother (the 1812 and 1816 acts write her Maria Josefa Gonzalez and Maria de Leon Gonzalez).

what: THE GODFATHER OF 1825 AND 1827 IS ALEJANDRO'S MATERNAL UNCLE AND HIS WIFE'S BROTHER-IN-LAW
the source: Uruguay, Civil Registration 1879-2020 - certified copy no. 776 of 1888 of the San Jose marriage act of 17 December 1815, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2Z-HQQP-2, index ark 1:1:XSX9-P277 - PLATE READ; found by searching the index for Marcos de Leon Gonzalez
result: 'D. MARCOS LEON GONZALEZ, NATURAL DE LAS ISLAS DE CANARIAS, HIJO LEGITIMO DE MARCIAL DE LEON GONZALEZ Y DE DA. ISABEL LORENZO ARAQUEA, CON DA. CASILDA FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ, NATURAL DE ESTA VILLA E HIJA LEGITIMA DE DON JUAN FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ Y DE DONA BARBARA SOTURA YA DIFUNTA'
what was already known: Marcos de Leon Gonzalez stood godfather at the 1825 wedding and the 1827 baptism, a surname that pointed at the groom's mother, and nothing more.
what the act says: HE IS THE BROTHER OF MARIA JOSEFA, THE GROOM'S MOTHER, AND THE HUSBAND OF CASILDA, THE BRIDE'S SISTER - THE TWO FAMILIES WERE LINKED TEN YEARS BEFORE THE WEDDING. Marcos and Maria Josefa are both Canary Islanders (Lanzarote is named for her), the children of Marcial de Leon Gonzalez and Isabel Lorenzo Araquea. Their niece Maria Casilda was named for his wife. And Barbara Sotura was DEAD by December 1815, so Barbara Sotura, named as a grandmother in the later baptisms, had long been dead.

what: *** MARIA LERENA'S HUSBAND IS RAMON FERNANDEZ, HER FIRST COUSIN; SOCORRO AND SERAPIO WERE THE GODPARENTS OF THEIR DAUGHTER ***
the source: Santisima Trinidad, Baptism Records 1848-1857, film 008163892, image 229, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F34L-N - *** PLATE READ ***; found by stepping through the volume and scanning each image's machine index for Lerena-like names
result: *** 'MARIA DEL CARMEN, QUE NACIO EL DIA DIEZ Y SEIS DEL QUE RIGE, E HIJA LEGITIMA DE RAMON FERNANDEZ Y DE MARIA LERENA, NATURALES Y VECINOS DE ESTA PARROQUIA. ABS. PAT.S MANUEL FERNANDEZ Y MARIA DE LOS REYES GONZALES, MAT.S D.N ALEJANDRO LERENA Y D.A MARGARITA FERNANDEZ. PADRINOS SERAPIO FERNANDEZ Y SOCORRO LERENA' (19 JULY 1857) ***
what was already known: Maria Lerena de Fernandez was a widow of the 1892 death act and her husband was not named.
what the act says: Her husband is a son of Manuel Fernandez Alvarez, the brother of Margarita Fernandez Alvarez, so two Lerena sisters married two Fernandez brothers who were their first cousins: Maria Lerena married Ramon Fernandez, and Socorro Lerena married Serapio Fernandez. The same scan found Estefania Lerena as a godmother at Trinidad in October 1850, beside Ramon Fernandez, and Clara Lerena as a godmother there in 1852. The scan was for the baptism of Vitalino Lerena, 1849-1857, and found none. The dispensation for Maria Lerena and Ramon Fernandez was not found that day; it was found on 19 October 2026 and is the row below.

what: *** MARIA LERENA, SAID TO BE 24, AND RAMON FERNANDEZ, 21: THEIR DISPENSATION AS FIRST COUSINS, ASKED FOR BY HIS FATHER ***
the source: Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records 1852-1855, film 007713344, item 3, images 162-167, expediente no. 15 of 1853; petition ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-T9B1-K, diagram ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-TS33-3 - the petition, the cover and the diagram *** PLATE READ ***; found by a full-text search for the two names
result: The cover reads 'Don Manuel Fernandez por su hijo Ramon, solicita ... dispensa del impedimento canonico de parentesco ... con Maria Lerena: parroquia de Porongos' (the second degree of consanguinity, by the transverse line); the petition 'mi hijo Ramon, soltero, de edad de veinte y un anos' and 'mi sobrina Maria Lerena, de edad de veinte y cuatro anos, natural de San Jose ... hija legitima de Alexandro Lerena y Margarita Fernandez, que es mi hermana'; the diagram dated 7 September 1853 puts Juan Fernandez Alvarez and Barbara Sotura at the apex, their children Manuel and Margarita below as 'hermanos, 1.o g.o', and Ramon and Maria below those as 'primos hermanos, 2.o g.o'
what was already known: The christening of their daughter in July 1857 named Ramon Fernandez as Maria Lerena's husband and a son of Manuel Fernandez and Maria de los Reyes Gonzalez; the dispensation itself had not been found.
what the act says: The first cousins' own papers state the kinship that the register had worked out from baptisms: Manuel Fernandez Alvarez and Margarita Fernandez Alvarez, brother and sister, children of Juan Fernandez Alvarez and Barbara Sotura, are the father of Ramon and the mother of Maria. Ramon, 21, was born and lived in the Puntas de San Jose district of the Trinidad parish; Maria, said to be 24 although her baptism puts her birth on or before 11 April 1827, was from San Jose and lived in the countryside of the same parish. Manuel gave the causes: she was past 24, lived in an unpopulated place, had no dowry, and her parents had nine children, four of them girls - where this register names five children of this couple. The Provisor General granted the dispensation at Montevideo on 7 September 1853, conditional on three witnesses before the parish priest and a penance of three pounds of wax each. The grant and the penance are read from FamilySearch's machine transcript, not from the plate. Not found: the marriage act itself (between September 1853 and July 1857), and the other four children.

what: *** RAMON FERNANDEZ DIED ON 27 OCTOBER 1887, AND THEIR SON RAMON MARRIED IN 1894 ***
the source: Trinidad civil Death Records 1885-1888, act no. 93, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-W7SP-H; Trinidad Religious Marriage Records 1875-1895 (film 008163895), act of 18 October 1894, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-V131; Flores civil acts of 1902, arks 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-W7HK-6 and 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-Q6JJ - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPTS READ, PLATES NOT OPENED ***; found in the full-text list of the 1853 dispensation search
result: The civil record of 27 October 1887 reads 'Don Ramon Fernandez, oriental, de cincuenta y seis anos de edad, casado, con Dona Maria Lerena, Oriental, de cincuenta y ocho anos de edad; de cuyo matrimonio existen tres hijos mayores de edad', declared by Servando Gonzalez 'por encargo de la esposa'; the marriage act of 18 October 1894 reads 'Don Ramon Fernandez Oriental, soltero, de treinta y cuatro anos de edad, hijo legitimo de Don Ramon Fernandez de Dona Maria Lerena; con Dona Maria Serna'; the births and deaths of 1902 name 'Abuelos paternos: Don Ramon Fernandez, y dona Maria Lerena fallecidos'.
what was already known: Maria Lerena was a widow in 1892 and her husband Ramon Fernandez was known from his daughter's baptism of 1857 and the dispensation of 1853; neither his end nor any child but Maria del Carmen was held.
what the act says: Ramon Fernandez died at the Puntas de San Jose on 27 October 1887 aged 56, so Maria Lerena had been a widow for four and a half years in 1892, and her brother-in-law Servando Gonzalez made the declaration. They had three grown children: Maria del Carmen (born 1857), Ramon the younger (born about 1860, a merchant at the Costa del Sarandi, who married Maria Serna at Trinidad in 1894) and one not found. Ramon the younger had a son on 27 February 1902, Ramon Maria Fernandez, whose mother had gone by then, and who lived twenty-two days; Bernabe Lerena witnessed the birth and Manuel Vaquero, a procurador said to be 'de la familia', the death. A Ramon Fernandez and a Maria Lerena also stand as godparents at Trinidad in 1868, 1879 and 1886 (the last for the child of Serapio Fernandez and Antonina Lerena) and as witnesses in 1877; these are very likely the couple and not proved. Not found: the third child, the baptisms of the children, and the marriage of Ramon Fernandez and Maria Lerena itself.

what: *** THE BAPTISMS OF THE FAMILY AT TRINIDAD, 1858 TO 1866 ***
the source: Trinidad, Baptism Records October 1857 - August 1866 (film 008163892, item 3, 238 images), all 238 images stepped through; the entries of the son of 1859 (image 62, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F34Y-H) and the son of 1866 (image 221, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3CD-6) and of a Vaquero child (image 134, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3CR-K) are the ones that name the couple and her sister - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPTS, SIX PLATES OPENED ***
result: The entries read 'Ramon de la Asuncion Fernandez que nacio el quatorce de este mismo mes y ano, hijo legitimo de Ramon Fernandez y de Maria Llerena, Orientales', 'Jesus Modesto del Carmen que nacio el 14 del presente, hijo legitimo de Don Ramon Fernandez y Dona Maria Lerena, naturales de esta Parroquia', and 'Manuel Yndalejio Vaquero que nacio el veinte y uno de Mayo de este mismo ano, hijo legitimo de Manuel Vaquero y de Natalia Lerena'.
what was already known: Ramon Fernandez and Maria Lerena had a daughter, Maria del Carmen, in 1857 and a son, Ramon, known from his marriage of 1894 and a civil record of 1911 as born in 1859 or 1860; the third grown child of 1887 was not known; and the fourth daughter of the household of Alejandro and Margarita, counted in the petition of 1853, was not named.
what the act says: Ramon the younger was born on 14 August 1859 and christened on the 19th with his father's parents as godparents, and a third child, Jesus Modesto del Carmen, was born in January 1866, twenty-one in January 1887 and so one of the 'tres hijos mayores de edad'. The fourth daughter is Natalia, who married Manuel Vaquero: she was godmother with Ramon Fernandez in 1858 and her son Manuel Indalecio, born 21 May 1862, had Alejandro and Margarita as godparents; he is very likely the procurador Manuel Vaquero called a relative in 1892 and 1902. The same volume holds twenty more baptisms of the sibship's children between 1858 and 1866, from the machine transcript: five of Alejandro the younger and Severa Fernandez, four of Serapio Fernandez and Socorro Lerena, four of Bernabe Lerena and Casimira Pelaez, four of Servando Gonzalez and Estefania Lerena and one of the household of Juan Pedro Pelaez; each is now a person in the register, with the entry's wording; all from the machine transcript. A second Ramon Fernandez, married to a Maria Teresa, appears in the same volume as godparent in 1863 and 1864 and as father of a daughter in 1862: not this couple.

what: *** NATALIA LERENA'S PARENTS ARE NAMED; HER SON IS THE PROCURADOR, MANUEL VAQUERO ***
the source: San Jose Baptism Records September 1862 - December 1865, entry of 5 March 1864, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-C9XF-7; Marriage Dispensation Records 1857-1860, expediente no. 440 of July 1861, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-VWH8-N; Flores Death Records 1888-1917, acts of 11 March 1889, 10 July 1891 and 29 August 1902, arks 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-QC2V, 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-QW9W and 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-Q7GQ - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPTS ***; found by a full-text search for Manuel Vaquero and Natalia Lerena
result: The baptism of 5 March 1864 reads 'Alejandra Justa ... hija legitima de D. Manuel Vaquero y de Dona Natalia Lerena; abuelos pat. D. Pedro y Dona Manuela Muniz; Mat. D. Alejandro y Dona Margarita Fernandez'; the dispensation of 4 July 1861 'contraer matrimonio con Dona Natalia Lerena, vecina del Pueblo de la SSma. Trinidad en Porongos'; the act of 11 March 1889 'el finado era casado con dona Natalia Lerena, de cuyo matrimonio queda su hijo llamado Manuel Vaquero'.
what was already known: Natalia Lerena had been placed as the fourth daughter of the 1853 petition from two Trinidad baptisms, with her parentage inferred from the godparents.
what the act says: Natalia Lerena's parents are written down: the maternal grandparents of her daughter are Alejandro and Margarita Fernandez. Her husband Manuel Vaquero asked in July 1861 for the banns to be dispensed and married her in the second half of that year; he was born about 1835, a hacendado at Cerro Colorado, son of Pedro Vaquero and Manuela Muniz, and ended on 11 March 1889 leaving one son, Manuel Vaquero. That son, born 21 May 1862, is the procurador Manuel Vaquero who was twenty-nine in 1891 and forty in 1902, and who signed the civil acts of his aunt Maria Lerena's household. A nephew of Natalia Lerena, a hacendado of Cerro Colorado, was the first declarant of that act. A daughter, Alejandra Justa, was born on 26 February 1864. Not found: the marriage act itself, and the baptism and the end of Natalia Lerena.

what: *** A SIXTH CHILD OF ALEJANDRO AND MARGARITA, AND BERNABE'S WIFE FOUND AT HER BAPTISM ***
the source: San Jose Baptism Records 1836-1840, entries of 1838, 26 May 1839 and 11 May 1840, arks 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D9PH-2, 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D9P3-X, 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D9P7-W; San Jose Baptism Records January 1841 - May 1869, entry of 3 April 1841, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D9PM-8 - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPTS ***; found by a full-text search with the San Jose place filter
result: The entry of 1838 reads 'a Ramon Inocencio que nacio el veinte y ocho de Julio proxime pasado, hijo legitimo de Alexandro [Lerena] y Margarita Fernandez: abuelos paternos Ramon y Maria Gonzalez: maternos Juan y Barbara Satura'; that of 3 April 1841, 'que nacio el diez y nueve de Marzo proximo pasado, hija legitima de Juan Pedro Pelaes y de Antonina Isabel Lerena'.
what was already known: Alejandro and Margarita were known to have had Maria Casilda, Alejandro, Estefania, Socorro, Natalia and Bernabe between 1827 and 1836; Casimira Pelaez, Bernabe's wife, had only an age of about fifty-six in 1897.
what the act says: A son, Ramon Inocencio, was born on 28 July 1838, after Bernabe, which makes seven of the nine children of the 1853 petition. Casimira Pelaez, whom Bernabe married in 1858 as his first cousin, was born on 19 March 1841 to Juan Pedro Pelaez and Antonina Isabel Lerena, a sister of Alejandro; her baptism gives the name Casimira Josefa that her mother's death act of 1911 uses. The same volumes show that Juan Fernandez and Barbara Sotura also had a son, Esteban Fernandez Alvarez, and that Alejandro Lerena had a sister Isabel Lerena. Natalia Lerena's own baptism was found the same day, in the volume of 1828-1836 (born 15 May 1834); it had been missed because the priest wrote the surname 'Ledena'.

what: *** THE FAMILY WAS AT TRINIDAD BY 1843, AND BURIED A BABY SON THERE IN MARCH 1844 ***
the source: Trinidad Baptism Records January 1843 - March 1848, all 43 images; the entries of 10 April 1843 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3H8-X), March 1844 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3HF-K) and 18 June 1847 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3H8-Y) - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPTS ***; found by a full-text search for Barbara Sotura and Margarita Fernandez in Flores
result: The entries read, in the machine transcript, that Alejandro Lerena and Margarita Fernandez (the surname written 'Herena') were godparents on 10 April 1843; that a child of theirs, Eugenio Lerena Fernandez, was baptised in March 1844, born on the 26th of February, the parents 'de S. Jose y vecinos de este Pueblo' and the godmother 'Mariquita' Lerena; and that on 18 June 1847 they were godparents of 'Margarita Antonia', daughter of Manuel Fernandez and Maria de los Reyes Gonzalez.
what was already known: The family was known at San Jose to 1840 and at Trinidad from the dispensations of the 1850s; the years between were a gap.
what the act says: Alejandro and Margarita were living at Trinidad by April 1843, and a son, Eugenio Lerena Fernandez, was born there on 26 February 1844, baptised at the start of March and buried on 3 March, a few days old (Trinidad Religious Death Records January 1835 - May 1860, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-23WL-4); he is not one of the nine children of the 1853 petition, who were all living then. An earlier version of this row, written the same day, gave his birth as 26 March and called him the eighth of the nine: that is withdrawn. The godmother 'Mariquita Lerena' is probably Maria, then seventeen. Manuel Fernandez and Maria de los Reyes Gonzalez were at Trinidad too, 'naturales de San Jose', and had a son Juan Crisostomo in January 1844 and a daughter Margarita Antonia in June 1847, whose godparents were Alejandro and Margarita. The earlier machine-index scan of the neighbouring volume missed two spellings of the surname; this one was read in full. Not found: the ninth child, and the baptisms of the 1850s that carry those spellings.

what: *** THE PARENTS OF A HACENDADO OF CERRO COLORADO ARE NAMED: ALEJANDRO THE YOUNGER AND SEVERA FERNANDEZ ***
the source: Trinidad Baptism Records 1848-1857, entry of 19 September 1855, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3HM-F; Trinidad Religious Marriage Records 1875-1895, act of 10 January 1884, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-V1CP; Flores Death Records 1888-1917, civil act of 4 April 1904, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-QC4X - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPTS ***; found by the record index and a full-text search
result: The baptism of 19 September 1855 reads, in the machine transcript, that a child christened Cipriano Pio, born on the sixteenth, was the legitimate son of Alejandro Lerena and Severa Fernandez; the marriage act of 10 January 1884 gives 'hijo legitimo de Don Alejandro y de Dona Severa Fernandez'; and the civil act of 4 April 1904, signed by Pio Cipriano Lerena, calls his parents 'ambos orientales, fallecidos'.
what was already known: Pio C. Lerena, a hacendado of Cerro Colorado, was known from an index record naming his parents as an Alejandro and a Severa Fernandez, and from the act of 1889 in which he is the nephew of Natalia Lerena's husband; whether his father was Alejandro Lerena the younger was not established.
what the act says: Pio Cipriano Lerena was born on 16 September 1855 at Trinidad and baptised on the 19th, the son of Alejandro Lerena the younger and Severa Fernandez, with his grandparents Alejandro and Margarita as godparents. He married Bernardina Harrison on 10 January 1884, and in April 1904 declared the death of a week-old son, Sixto Doroteo Lerena, naming both his own parents as dead. A daughter of the same parents, born on 1 October 1856, had Ramon Fernandez and Maria Lerena as godparents. Not found: the end of Pio Cipriano Lerena, and the plate of any of these acts.

what: *** THE SAN JOSE VOLUME OF 1828-1835 NAMES NO MORE CHILDREN OF ALEJANDRO AND MARGARITA, BUT A WHOLE FAMILY AROUND THEM ***
the source: San Jose Baptism Records May 1828 - January 1836, all 191 images re-read with a spelling-tolerant search; the entries of 1 May 1828 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D9L5-H) and of 1829-1835 (arks 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D95N-M, 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D95Z-F, 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D95W-Q, 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D957-6, 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D9PB-P, 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D95Q-9, 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D9PG-T, 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D9PN-G) - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPTS ***
result: The entry of 1 May 1828 reads 'Pedro Francisco que nacio el veinte y nueve de Abril, hijo legitimo de Francisco Fernandez y Clara Lerena: Abuelos Paternos Juan, y Barbara Solera: Maternos Ramon y Maria de Leon Gonzalez'.
what was already known: Alejandro Lerena's sister Clara, godmother in 1829, was known only as a godmother; the Fernandez side was known as Margarita and Casilda, with Maria, Manuel and Esteban found in other acts.
what the act says: Clara Lerena was the wife of Francisco Fernandez, a brother of Margarita, so two Lerena siblings married a Fernandez brother and sister; their son Pedro Francisco was born on 29 April 1828. Juan Fernandez and Barbara Sotura had at least seven children - Maria, Margarita, Casilda, Josefa, Manuel, Francisco and Esteban - and the baptisms of Josefa's four, Casilda's three and Maria's one are in this volume. The only children of Alejandro and Margarita in it are those already known: Alejandro, Estefania, Socorro and Natalia, so the re-read with the wider spellings found no child that the first scan missed. [Superseded 26 October 2026: Isaac Filomeno, baptised at San Jose in June 1845, is a ninth child of the couple; the count of missing children is open.] Not found at the time: the missing two of the nine, who must be in the Trinidad volume of 1848-1857, or born between 1840 and 1848.

what: *** THE TRINIDAD VOLUME OF 1848-1857 NAMES A FIRST CHILD OF RAMON FERNANDEZ AND MARIA LERENA, A SON OF ANTONINA LERENA, AND NO CHILD OF ALEJANDRO AND MARGARITA ***
the source: Santisima Trinidad Baptism Records 1848-1857, all 194 images re-read with a spelling-tolerant search; the entries of 18 August 1855 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F34B-N), 16 August 1856 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3HS-W), 7 June 1855 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3H9-X), January 1849 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3H4-K) and February 1852 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3HQ-J) - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPTS ***
result: The entry of 18 August 1855 names the child's parents as the husband Ramon Fernandez (m. Maria Lerena) and his wife, the mother's surname written Leiena, with Margarita Fernandez by proxy as godmother.
what was already known: The first read of this volume (on the machine's index of Lerena-like names) held three of the Lerena baptisms of 1855 to 1857; the first child of Ramon and Maria was not found because the mother is written Leiena.
what the act says: Ramon FERNANDEZ (m. Maria Lerena) and Maria LERENA (m. FERNANDEZ, d. 1892 Trinidad) had a son Eusebio Ramon FERNANDEZ Lerena (b. 1855, Trinidad), baptised on 18 August 1855, before Maria del Carmen of 1857 and the younger Ramon of 1859, so their marriage, dispensed on 7 September 1853, was celebrated before the summer of 1855. Juan PELAEZ (m. Antonina LERENA) and Antonina LERENA (the elder, m. Juan PELAEZ) had a son, Alejandro Pablo PELAEZ Lerena (b. 1856, Trinidad), born on 30 June 1856, with Alejandro LERENA (the elder, m. Margarita Fernandez Alvarez) and Margarita FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ (wife of Alejandro LERENA the elder) as godparents. A baptism of 7 June 1855, read at the plate, is that of Julio Servando del Carmen GONZALEZ Lerena (b. 1855, Trinidad), a son of Servando GONZALEZ (m. Estefania Lerena) and Estefania LERENA (m. Servando GONZALEZ). The volume holds no child of Alejandro the elder and Margarita: [Superseded 26 October 2026: see Isaac Filomeno, baptised at San Jose in June 1845.] the two still missing of the nine, if they were born after 1840, were baptised before January 1849 or after October 1857.

what: *** THE TRINIDAD VOLUME OF 1857-1866 RE-READ: ONE MORE CHILD OF ALEJANDRO THE YOUNGER, TWO MORE OF RAMON FERNANDEZ AND MARIA LERENA, AND A MAURICIO LERENA WITH A WIFE PETRONA AGUILAR ***
the source: Santisima Trinidad Baptism Records October 1857 - August 1866, all 238 images re-read with a spelling-tolerant search; the entries of 7 October 1858 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F342-Q), 22 May 1862 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3CR-7), 4 March 1864 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3CF-2), 15 June 1865 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3CJ-5) and 21 June 1866 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3CZ-1) - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPTS ***
result: The entry of 4 March 1864 reads 'Modesta Carmelita ... hija legitima de Ramon Fernandez y de Maria Serena; Abuelos Paternos Manuel Fernandez y Reyes; Maternos Alexandro Lerena y Margarita Fernandez'.
what was already known: The first walk of this volume (19 October) read the Lerena, Llerena, Lorena and Serena spellings and held fifteen cousin-children; it missed the entries where the mother is written 'Lorena Santiles' or 'Maria Serena', the father 'Serenas' in a later child, and the Mauricio written 'Macericio Serena' or 'Perena'.
what the act says: Alejandro LERENA (the younger, m.1 Isidora Chourino, m.2 Severa Fernandez 1854) and Severa FERNANDEZ (m. Alejandro LERENA the younger, 1854) had a son Pedro Segundo Gregorio in 1865, the last of the children held for the couple, whose baptisms run from 1855 to 1865. Ramon FERNANDEZ (m. Maria Lerena) and Maria LERENA (m. FERNANDEZ, d. 1892 Trinidad) had six children baptised between 1855 and 1866, which corrects the third child that the row of Jesus Modesto del Carmen FERNANDEZ Lerena (b. 1866, Trinidad) had called him. A Mauricio Lerena and Petrona AGUILAR (m. Mauricio Lerena, Trinidad 1866) are godparents twice in 1866 and parents of Paula Gregoria LERENA Aguilar (b. 1866, Trinidad); Mauricio LERENA (of Colla/Rosario, m. Casimira Montano 1837) and Dona Casimira MONTANO (wife of Mauricio LERENA) had a son at Trinidad in November 1863. No child of Alejandro the elder and Margarita is in the volume.

what: *** THE TRINIDAD VOLUME OF 1843-1848 RE-READ: AN ENSLAVED WOMAN WRITTEN BARBARA LLERENA ***
the source: Santisima Trinidad Baptism Records January 1843 - March 1848, all 43 images re-read with a spelling-tolerant search; the entries of 29 October 1843 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3H5-D) and June 1846 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-F3HY-T) - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPT ***
result: The entry of 29 October 1843 gives Fructuosa, born 26 October, as the natural daughter of Barbara Llerena, 'esclava, vecina de este Pueblo'.
what was already known: The first walk of the volume (19 October) held Eugenio, Juan Crisostomo and Margarita Antonia; it did not read the enslaved woman or the godmother of 1846.
what the act says: A woman held as a slave at Trinidad in 1843 is written with the surname of the family; she is probably the Barbara who was held by Alejandro Lerena and who bore a son at San Jose in 1846, which the entry of 1843 does not say. Estefania LERENA (m. Servando GONZALEZ) was godmother at fifteen in June 1846. The volume holds no other child of Alejandro and Margarita.

what: *** A CHILD OF ALEJANDRO AND MARGARITA BAPTISED AT SAN JOSE IN JUNE 1845: ISAAC FILOMENO ***
the source: San Jose de Mayo Baptism Records January 1841 - May 1869 (entries to 1847), all 152 images read with a spelling-tolerant search; the entry of 27 June 1845, image 110 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSKH-D9GJ-5) - *** PLATE READ ***
result: The entry of 27 June 1845 names the child as Isaac Filomeno, born on the third of the month, and his parents as the husband Alejandro LERENA (the elder, m. Margarita Fernandez Alvarez), the surname written Llerena, and Margarita FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ (wife of Alejandro LERENA the elder), with a Larriera and a Morales as godparents.
what was already known: Eight children of the couple were held: Maria Casilda (1827), Alejandro (1829), Estefania (1831), Socorro (1832), Natalia (1834), Bernabe (1836), Ramon Inocencio (1838) and Eugenio (1844, buried a few days old), against the nine of the petition of 1853; the volumes of 1828-1836, 1836-1840 and 1843-1866 had been read for the others and had none.
what the act says: Alejandro LERENA (the elder, m. Margarita Fernandez Alvarez) and Margarita FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ (wife of Alejandro LERENA the elder) had a child baptised at San Jose in 1845, Ysaac LERENA (of Trinidad), so nine children are now known to have been baptised, one of whom, Eugenio, lived days. [Added 26 October 2026: Isaac lived - he is the Ysaac LERENA of Trinidad, a stockbreeder and carpenter, husband of Adelaida GAZO and father of four held children, whose son's baptism of 1880 names Alejandro and Margarita Fernandez as his grandparents.] No child of the couple is now known to be missing. The same volume holds Carmelo Belisario in 1842 and Tomasa Margarita in 1846, children of Mauricio LERENA (of Colla/Rosario, m. Casimira Montano 1837).

what: *** THE SAN JOSE VOLUME OF 1822-1828 HAS A YOUNGER SISTER OF THE HUSBAND AND NO CHILD OF 1826 ***
the source: San Jose Baptism Records July 1822 - April 1828, images 55-126 read with a spelling-tolerant search; the entries of 20 May 1825 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-CS95-4), September 1826 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-CS9Y-M), October 1826 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-CS9R-1) and 29 November 1827 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-CS9P-P) - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPTS ***
result: The entry of 20 May 1825 baptises a newborn girl, the child of the Rosario-Colla couple, the mother written with her surname Gonzalez, and names the priest and a godmother whose surname the machine writes Perena.
what was already known: Alejandro's sister Clara was known as a godmother at San Jose in 1829, and the parents Ramon Lerena and Maria Josefa Gonzalez from the baptisms of 1812 to 1821 at Montevideo and from Alejandro's marriage act.
what the act says: Ramon LERENA (of Rosario-Colla, fl. 1794-1820) and Maria Josefa GONZALEZ (wife of Ramon LERENA of Colla) had a daughter baptised at San Jose on 20 May 1825, Pascual Maria Cruz LERENA Gonzalez (bapt. 1825, San Jose), with Clara LERENA (madrina, San Jose 1829) as godmother, so Clara was in the family's circle at San Jose four months before Alejandro's marriage. The volume holds no child of Alejandro and Margarita before Maria Casilda of April 1827. Three cousins were baptised in 1826 and 1827, children of Juan ALVAREZ (m. Josefa Fernandez) and Josefa FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ (m. Juan Alvarez), and of Marcos de LEON GONZALEZ (godfather, 1825) and Casilda FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ (m. Marcos de Leon Gonzalez 1815).

what: *** ESTEFANIA LERENA WAS MARRIED ON 13 JULY 1853, AND A CERTIFIED COPY OF 1892 QUOTES THE ENTRY ***
the source: Montevideo Marriage Records January - November 1892, image 107 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2Z-ZQ9R-C), the copy of the act of Santisima Trinidad, Libro segundo de matrimonios, folio 13 - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPT ***
result: The entry of 13 July 1853 marries Don Servando Gonzalez, son of Juan Nepomuceno GONZALEZ (father of Servando) and Manuela MUNIZ (m. Juan Nepomuceno Gonzalez), to Dona Estefania Lerena, daughter of Don Alejandro and Dona Margarita Fernandez, and names the bride's parents as the witnesses.
what was already known: Estefania's marriage had no date and no act in the register; it was known from her children, and her parents were last placed at Trinidad in August 1855.
what the act says: Servando GONZALEZ (m. Estefania Lerena) and Estefania LERENA (m. Servando GONZALEZ) married at Trinidad on 13 July 1853, with Alejandro LERENA (the elder, m. Margarita Fernandez Alvarez) and Margarita FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ (wife of Alejandro LERENA the elder) as witnesses, and the first child Julio Servando del Carmen GONZALEZ Lerena (b. 1855, Trinidad) was born on 1 February 1855. The same book (Libro segundo de matrimonios of Trinidad) would hold the marriage of Ramon FERNANDEZ (m. Maria Lerena) and Maria LERENA (m. FERNANDEZ, d. 1892 Trinidad), dispensed on 7 September 1853, and has not yet been found.

what: *** NATALIA LERENA WAS MARRIED ON 5 AUGUST 1861, AND THE ENTRY IS QUOTED IN A COPY OF 1898 ***
the source: Montevideo Marriage Records 1898-1899, image 114 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2Z-HQ9Y-2), the copy of the Trinidad entry - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPT ***
result: The entry marries Manuel VAQUERO (m. Natalia Lerena), twenty-seven, born at San Jose, son of the late Pedro VAQUERO (father of Manuel Vaquero) and of Manuela MUNIZ (wife of Pedro Vaquero), to Natalia LERENA (m. Manuel Vaquero), twenty-seven, born at San Jose, daughter of Alejandro and Margarita Fernandez, with her parents as witnesses.
what was already known: Natalia's marriage had no entry in the register; she was known from her baptism, her children and the Vaquero acts.
what the act says: Manuel VAQUERO (m. Natalia Lerena) and Natalia LERENA (m. Manuel Vaquero) married at Trinidad on 5 August 1861 with Alejandro LERENA (the elder, m. Margarita Fernandez Alvarez) and Margarita FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ (wife of Alejandro LERENA the elder) as witnesses, eight years after her sister Estefania LERENA (m. Servando GONZALEZ) married Servando GONZALEZ (m. Estefania Lerena). The two grooms' mothers are both Manuela Muniz, which may make the two grooms half-brothers; the register keeps the two Manuelas apart for now.

what: *** MARGARITA ANTONIA FERNANDEZ IS FOUND AGAIN: A DISPENSATION PETITION OF 17 JUNE 1865 ***
the source: Marriage Dispensation Records 1864-1867, expediente no. 511 (arks 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-5BJY, 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-5975-H, 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-5BNH, 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-5BNL) - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPT ***
result: Jose Pedro Maciel, born in the department of San Jose, asks the Cura Vicario at Trinidad to examine witnesses so that he may marry Margarita Fernandez, born in the parish, to whom he is tied in the third degree by the transverse line; the witnesses name her parents Manuel and Maria de los Reyes Gonzalez and the grandparents on both sides.
what was already known: Margarita Antonia FERNANDEZ Gonzalez (b. 1847, Trinidad) was known only from her baptism of 1847, 'not found afterwards'.
what the act says: She is eighteen in June 1865 and wants to marry a third cousin of the Pelaez line, Jose Pedro MACIEL (suitor of Margarita Antonia Fernandez, 1865), son of Eusebio MACIEL (father of Jose Pedro Maciel) and Bonifacia PELAEZ (wife of Eusebio Maciel). Her maternal grandparents are Patricio GONZALEZ (father of Maria de los Reyes) and Juana CABALLERO (wife of Patricio Gonzalez). Whether the dispensation was granted and the marriage made is not read. A Laureana Maciel stands proxy for her aunt Margarita Fernandez Alvarez at Trinidad in 1855.

what: *** THE ELDER BERNABE OF THE 1911 DIAGRAM IS THE BERNABE OF TRINIDAD ***
the source: Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records of 1911, the diagram (film 007713362, image 02473, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-GS3N-1 - plate read), with the double wedding of 25 April 1889 at Trinidad and the baptisms of Bernabe's children
result: The diagram puts one Bernabe Lerena at the apex, with lines down to Bernabe, who married Florinda Cardozo, and to Maria, who married Eliseo Cardozo.
what was already known: The register had held the apex as a person of his own, unattached, with the Bernabe of Trinidad kept apart as a 'candidate pair'; the test written for them was a record naming the Trinidad Bernabe's children.
what the act says: The 1889 act names Maria's parents as Bernabe LERENA (of Trinidad) and Dona Casimira PELAEZ (wife of Bernabe LERENA), and Maria is the Maria LERENA (m. Eliseo CARDOZO) of the diagram, so the apex is that Bernabe; the group of eleven people of the 1911 dispensation is now joined to the Trinidad family, and Custodio LERENA, the groom, is his grandson.

what: *** TWO GRANDCHILDREN OF ALEJANDRO THE YOUNGER WERE BAPTISED ON 15 JULY 1886, AND ONE NAMES A SON THE REGISTER DID NOT HOLD ***
the source: Santisima Trinidad Baptism Records 1886-1888, image 30 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-NQ7Y-G) - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPT ***
result: The entries give the parents and both sets of grandparents of Alejandro Pedro Pelaez (maternal grandparents Alejandro Florencio and Isidora) and of Antonio Amador Lerena (paternal grandparents Alejandro and Severa Fernandez).
what was already known: Alejandro Lerena the younger's sons known were Pio Cipriano, Venancio, Juan Ramon, Pilar Florencio and Pedro Segundo Gregorio; the register held a Gualberto Lerena who married Rosaura Alvarez with no parents.
what the act says: Gualberto LERENA (m. Rosaura Alvarez) is a son of Alejandro LERENA (the younger, m.1 Isidora Chourino, m.2 Severa Fernandez 1854) and Severa FERNANDEZ (m. Alejandro LERENA the younger, 1854), and his son Antonio Amador LERENA Alvarez (b. 1886, Trinidad) was born on 13 June 1886; Alejandro Pedro PELAEZ Lerena (b. 1886, Trinidad), born on 29 June 1886, is a son of Alejandrina LERENA (m. Balbino PELAEZ) and Malvino PELAEZ (son of Juan PELAEZ and Antonina LERENA).

what: *** A DAUGHTER OF ALEJANDRO THE YOUNGER AND SEVERA FERNANDEZ, MARRIED AT TRINIDAD ON 14 JULY 1877, FOUND IN THE MARRIAGE BOOK AND IN A COPY OF 1932 ***
the source: Santisima Trinidad Religious Marriage Records 1875-1895, image 25 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-V1YP) - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPT ***; and Uruguay Marriage Records 1931-1932, image 156 (folio 300, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2Z-Z7CP-G), the certified copy of 1932 - *** PLATE READ for the names, ages and witnesses ***
result: The entry of 14 July 1877 marries Don Francisco Lejeron, twenty-five, son of Francisco and Simona Guiteria, to Dona Laurencia Lerena, twenty, daughter of Don Alejandro Florencio and Dona Severa Fernandez, with Serapio Fernandez and Socorro Lerena as witnesses.
what was already known: The eight children of the couple baptised 1855-1865 and a ninth, Gualberto, from a baptism of 1886, were known; a daughter of twenty in 1877 was not, though the baptism of 13 October 1856 held as 'Sanscuria Remisia' may be hers.
what the act says: Laurencia LERENA Fernandez (b. c.1857, m. Francisco Lejeren 1877) is a daughter of Alejandro LERENA (the younger, m.1 Isidora Chourino, m.2 Severa Fernandez 1854) and Severa FERNANDEZ (m. Alejandro LERENA the younger, 1854), and her husband is Francisco LEJEREN (m. Laurencia Lerena 1877). [Corrected 26 October 2026: the machine transcript of the 1932 copy gave the year 1867, which put her birth seven years before her parents' dispensation of 1854; the original book of 1875-1895 has the entry in 1877, so there is no conflict.]

what: *** GUALBERTO LERENA'S MARRIAGE, 25 JUNE 1885: HE IS JUAN GUALBERTO, AND HIS WIFE'S PARENTS ARE NAMED ***
the source: Santisima Trinidad Religious Marriage Records 1875-1895, image 118 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-V1Q5) - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPT ***
result: The entry of 25 June 1885 authorises, with a dispensation of the third degree of consanguinity by the equal lateral line, the marriage of Gualberto LERENA (m. Rosaura Alvarez), twenty-three, son of Alejandro LERENA (the younger, m.1 Isidora Chourino, m.2 Severa Fernandez 1854) and Severa FERNANDEZ (m. Alejandro LERENA the younger, 1854), to Rosaura ALVAREZ (m. Gualberto LERENA), twenty-four, daughter of Juan Francisco ALVAREZ (father of Rosaura Alvarez) and Clara PELAEZ (wife of Juan Francisco Alvarez).
what was already known: Gualberto Lerena's marriage and his own parents were not held; the baptism of his son of 1886 gave the parents, and nothing gave a date.
what the act says: Gualberto LERENA (m. Rosaura Alvarez) married Rosaura ALVAREZ (m. Gualberto LERENA) on 25 June 1885; her parents are Juan Francisco ALVAREZ (father of Rosaura Alvarez) and Clara PELAEZ (wife of Juan Francisco Alvarez). He was born between June 1861 and June 1862, and is probably the Juan Ramon LERENA Fernandez (chr.1862) baptised on 18 July 1862; the baptism is a machine transcript and the plate would settle it.

what: *** ALEJANDRO THE YOUNGER DIED ON 5 MARCH 1867, AT THIRTY-EIGHT ***
the source: Santisima Trinidad Religious Death Records June 1860 - December 1872, image 70 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-23WF-5), the burial of 6 March 1867 - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPT ***
result: The entry buries in the public cemetery Alejandro LERENA (the younger, m.1 Isidora Chourino, m.2 Severa Fernandez 1854), who died the day before of an aneurysm at the age of thirty-eight, married to Severa FERNANDEZ (m. Alejandro LERENA the younger, 1854); the surname is written with an H.
what was already known: Alejandro Lerena the younger was known to be dead by 1904, from his son Pio's act, and by the death of his daughter Alejandrina's act of 1926, with no date.
what the act says: Alejandro LERENA (the younger, m.1 Isidora Chourino, m.2 Severa Fernandez 1854) died on 5 March 1867, when Pedro Segundo Gregorio, his last child held, was not two, and Severa FERNANDEZ (m. Alejandro LERENA the younger, 1854) was a widow from that day; his daughters Laurencia and Alejandrina married in 1877 and about 1870s with their father dead.

what: *** THE TRINIDAD DEATH REGISTER OF 1860-1872 HOLDS THREE CHILDREN WHO DID NOT LIVE, A FAMILY NOT PLACED, AND A WOMAN OF SIXTY BURIED IN DECEMBER 1869 ***
the source: Santisima Trinidad Religious Death Records June 1860 - December 1872, all 153 images read with a spelling-tolerant search; the burials of 6 March 1865 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-23WX-J), the end of January 1866 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-23WN-P), 14 April 1866 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-23W6-F), 25 February 1869 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-23WD-Z) and 21 December 1869 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-23WC-8) - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPTS ***
result: The entry of 21 December 1869 buries a Margarita of sixty, whose surname the machine breaks in two, who died the day before of a natural illness; the entry of 14 April 1866 buries Faustino Lerena, twenty-two, son of Don Gil Lerena and Dona Anastasia Santa Cruz.
what was already known: The deaths of Alejandro the elder, Margarita, Isidora Chourino and Maria Josefa Gonzalez were not held; the burials of 1835-1860 had been read for them and had nothing.
what the act says: Cecilia Socorro FERNANDEZ Lerena (chr.1862) died on 5 March 1865, Pablo VAQUERO Lerena (chr.1866) four days after his birth, and Camila LERENA Pelaez (b. c.1868, buried 1869), a daughter of Bernabe LERENA (of Trinidad), at three months; Faustino LERENA (son of Gil, buried 1866) belonged to a Lerena household of Gil LERENA (m. Anastasia Santa Cruz) and Anastasia SANTA CRUZ (m. Gil Lerena) that no act ties to the others; and the woman of sixty buried on 21 December 1869, whose name the plate gives as Margarita Lerena in the margin, is very likely Margarita FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ (wife of Alejandro LERENA the elder), who would then have died on 20 December 1869 and left her husband, if living, for the register of 1873 onward.

what: *** VITALINO LERENA IS THE NINTH CHILD OF ALEJANDRO AND MARGARITA ***
the source: Flores Death Records 1888-1917, image 125, act no. 4 of April 1898 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-Q7PZ) - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPT ***
result: The act records the death on 17 March 1898 of Alejandro J. Lerena, twenty-three, 'hijo legitimo de Vitalino Lerena, oriental, fallecido, y de Etcheverse, oriental; abuelos paternos Alejandro Lerena y Margarita Fernandez y maternos Juan Etcheverre y Marcelina Anibal'.
what was already known: Vitalino LERENA (of Trinidad) was held since September as a man fathering children at Trinidad in the 1870s, with a possible godfather's role in 1867, and no parents; the open item of the row was whose son he was.
what the act says: Vitalino LERENA (of Trinidad) is a son of Alejandro LERENA (the elder, m. Margarita Fernandez Alvarez) and Margarita FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ (wife of Alejandro LERENA the elder), and so the ninth living child of the nine of the petition of 1853; his wife is Dona Andrea ECHEVERRY (wife of Vitalino LERENA), and their son Alejandro J. LERENA Echeverry (b. c.1875, d. 1898) died at twenty-three.

what: *** CIPRIANO LERENA'S HOUSEHOLD: FOUR MORE CHILDREN, AND THE DEATH OF ONE IN 1912 ***
the source: Trinidad baptisms of 1881 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSJB-152S), 1888 (3:1:3Q9M-CS27-NQ7L-Y) and 1890 (3:1:3Q9M-CS27-NQ7F-6), and the San Gregorio death act of 2 October 1912 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-QWL7) - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPTS; the opening lines of the death act PLATE READ ***
result: The death act of 2 October 1912 records the death on 27 September at the Puntas de San Jose of 'Eliseo Lerena', thirty-two, married, a day-labourer, son of Don Cipriano Lerena, sixty-one, and of Dona Lauriana Beloque, dead; the declarant is his brother Ademar Lerena, twenty-six.
what was already known: Cipriano and Lauriana were held with seven children, Doroteo Donato, Maria Leonor, Juan Cipriano, Amabelia, Casto Lindolfo, Lauriana and Carmen Donata.
what the act says: Cipriano LERENA (of Trinidad), a son of Mauricio of Colla, and Dona Lauriana BELOQUI (wife of Cipriano LERENA) had also Viviano Eliseo LERENA Beloqui (b. 1880, d. 1912), who died on 27 September 1912, Ademar LERENA Beloqui (b. c.1886), Celestino Ismael LERENA Beloqui (b. 1888, Trinidad) and Donata Natalia LERENA Beloqui (b. 1889, Trinidad); Lauriana was dead by September 1912 and Cipriano a widower of sixty-one.

what: *** TWO CHILDREN OF CIPRIANO LERENA WERE MARRIED IN JANUARY AND MARCH 1906, AND THE SECOND CORRECTS THE REGISTER'S LUISA ***
the source: Santisima Trinidad Religious Marriage Records July 1898 - December 1912, images 94 and 95 (arks 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-VYH9 and 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-VY8M) - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPTS ***
result: The entries of 5 January and 1 March 1906 marry Doroteo Donato Lerena, thirty, son of Cipriano Lerena and Laureana Belloqui, to Valentina Sena, twenty-five, and Bonaventura Olivera, twenty-four, to Luisa Lerena, twenty-one, daughter of Cipriano and Lauriana Beloqui.
what was already known: The Luisa whose sons Ramon Paulino (1908) and Juan Pedro (1909) were christened at Trinidad had been guessed to be Luisa LERENA Alvarez (m. Clemente Bueno 1915), daughter of Pedro Gualberto LERENA Villademoros, an identification the rows themselves said was only possible.
what the act says: The Luisa of those children is Luisa LERENA Beloqui (b. c.1884, m. Buenaventura Olivera 1906), wife of Buenaventura OLIVERA (m. Luisa Lerena); Luisa LERENA Alvarez (m. Clemente Bueno 1915) is a daughter of Gualberto LERENA (m. Rosaura Alvarez), not of Pedro Gualberto LERENA Villademoros, and Doroteo Donato LERENA Beloqui, who married Valentina SENA (m. Doroteo Donato Lerena) on 5 January 1906, is Cipriano's eldest son.

what: *** ELISEO LERENA MARRIED A GIRL OF SIXTEEN AT PUNTAS DE SAN JOSE ON 1 MARCH 1911, AND HIS FATHER WAS ALREADY A WIDOWER ***
the source: Flores Marriage Records 1887-1930, image 90 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSKV-K3K9-P) - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPT ***
result: The civil act of 1 March 1911 marries Don Eliseo Lerena, a day-labourer, son of Don Cipriano Lerena, a widower and landowner, and of Dona Laureana Beloqui, dead, to Dona Clara A. Plaza, born 12 August 1894, daughter of Froilan Plaza, dead, and of Ezequiela Paven, a widow; the witnesses include Eliseo's brother Adelmar Lerena, twenty-five.
what was already known: Eliseo's death on 27 September 1912 was held from the act of his death; his marriage and wife were not.
what the act says: Viviano Eliseo LERENA Beloqui (b. 1880, d. 1912) was married to Clara A. PLAZA (m. Eliseo Lerena 1911), whose parents are Froilan PLAZA (father of Clara Plaza) and Ezequiela PAVEN (wife of Froilan Plaza), eighteen months before his death; Dona Lauriana BELOQUI (wife of Cipriano LERENA) had died before 1 March 1911. The act gives his birth as 12 September 1881 against the baptism of 1880; the baptism stands.

what: *** FERMIN LERENA IS A SON OF GIL LERENA AND ANASTASIA SANTA CRUZ, AND SO OF THE HOUSEHOLD WHOSE SON WAS BURIED IN 1866 ***
the source: Santisima Trinidad Baptism Records 1876-1879, image 67 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CSJB-1RKY) - the baptism of 17 May 1877; and Religious Death Records 1915-1923 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-23WP-W) - the burial of 28 June 1923 - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPTS ***
result: The baptism names the infant Faustino's paternal grandparents as Don Gil and Dona Anastasia Santa Cruz and his maternal grandparents as Don Antonio and a Dona Gonzalez; the burial of 28 June 1923 is of Paulina Barragan, seventy-one, married to Fermin Lerena.
what was already known: Fermin Lerena was held as one of six or seven men of a rare surname fathering children at Trinidad in the 1870s and 1880s, with no parents; Gil and Anastasia Santa Cruz were found on the burial of their son Faustino in 1866 and not placed.
what the act says: Fermin LERENA (of Trinidad) is a son of Gil LERENA (m. Anastasia Santa Cruz) and Anastasia SANTA CRUZ (m. Gil Lerena), a brother of Faustino LERENA (son of Gil, buried 1866), and the father of Faustino LERENA Barragan, born 18 March 1877; his wife Dona Paulina BARRAGAN (wife of Fermin LERENA) died on 27 June 1923. The Gil Lerena house is a second family at Trinidad that no act ties to Alejandro's or Mauricio's.

what: *** FLORENCIO AND AURORA ARE CHILDREN OF ALEJANDRO THE YOUNGER, AND TWO PHANTOM PARENTS ARE GONE ***
the source: Santisima Trinidad Baptism Records 1889-1894, image 110 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-NQ7C-N), the baptisms of 3 September 1891 - *** MACHINE TRANSCRIPT ***
result: The entry for Natalia Elena names her parents Florencio Lerena and Juana Recuero and her paternal grandparents Alejandro and Severa Fernandez; the entry for Casto Severino names his paternal grandparents Manuel and Natalia Lerena and his maternal grandparents Alejandro and Severa Fernandez.
what was already known: The register held 'Alejandro F. Lerena' and 'Natalia Lerena' from the Trinidad index as the parents of Aurora, a Lerena married to a Lerena, and kept Alejandro F. apart from the younger Alejandro on arithmetic.
what the act says: Alejandro LERENA (the younger, m.1 Isidora Chourino, m.2 Severa Fernandez 1854) and Severa FERNANDEZ (m. Alejandro LERENA the younger, 1854) are the parents of Aurora LERENA Fernandez (m. Manuel VAQUERO) and of Florencio LERENA (of Trinidad); Aurora married Manuel VAQUERO (m.
